title: add-websocket-delta-sync-and-replay-inspector-quickstart
author: Maya Chen
description:
Context: Developers asked for a compact quickstart demonstrating low-latency RAG patterns where incremental retrieval (delta sync) and streaming deltas to the client reduce token costs and improve editor-like UX. This PR adds a new quickstart that wires: 1) a small TypeScript server that accepts query sessions and exposes a websocket delta-sync channel, 2) a minimal dev 'Replay Inspector' web UI that visualizes incoming retrieval deltas and embedding deltas, and 3) typed tool-contract stubs, a smoke e2e replay harness, and CI checks. Motivation: Many teams prototype RAG with full re-runs per message. For editor/assistant flows this causes repetitive retrieval and KV-work; delta-sync keeps KV/embedding state incremental and makes prefix caching obvious to engineers. The quickstart is intended as:
- Fast onboarding: clone, docker-compose up (or npm run dev)
- Clear examples: server stream -> client browser inspector -> replay harness
- Diagnostic-first: inspector surfaces retrieval hits, embedding similarity traces, and token/latency counters
Checklist: [x] add websocket delta-sync server and client library samples [x] add dev inspector UI and telemetry probes [x] add typed TS tool-contracts and schema examples [x] add CI smoke e2e & lint [x] document runbook and architecture diagram [x] add replay harness to reproduce incidents
How to run locally: 1) cd quickstarts/delta-sync 2) npm ci && npm run build 3) npm run start:dev (starts server + indexer) 4) open dev-inspector at http://localhost:8080 and connect a session 5) run examples/replay-harness to emit recorded user steps
Notes on design decisions:
- Websocket channel carries small JSON 'deltas' (retrieval-add, cache-hit, embedding-update, token-chunk) to keep messages idempotent and replayable.
- The indexer in this quickstart is intentionally in-process and keyed for clarity; production users should swap in Redwood's offline indexer or a managed vector DB.
- Typed tool-contracts are provided to show how structured tool-calling can interleave with deltas (see typed-contracts/tool-contracts.ts).
Related Linear: ["ENG-3412", "ENG-3480"]. Related docs: docs/devguides/delta-sync.md. Migration notes: no breaking API changes in Redwood; this is an additive set of samples and docs.

release_notes: Added 'delta-sync' quickstart demonstrating websocket-based incremental retrieval and a Replay Inspector developer UI. Includes typed tool-contract examples and a replay harness for deterministic e2e smoke tests. Useful for prototyping low-latency RAG flows and debugging retrieval/embedding behavior.
